decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts sit at the core of the firm's packaging-wafer competence and serve growing semiconductor demand, so results likely meet aspirations.
Carrier wafers for thin and small-wafer handling match the firm's stated direction of reusable carriers, and an expanding market gives no shortfall that would trigger search.
The Cu-interposer was launched prominently at SEMICON as a strategic technology, and the firm's slack in a growing industry allows it to carry this product while its results are still uncertain.
The off-the-shelf brand uses existing products and processes at low incremental cost, broadens access to customers and is likely to perform satisfactorily.
Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core and their results are more uncertain, but growing turnover provides enough slack to keep them for now.
